nodes.roadmap_statement:
The tubes are essentially distinct. For every $\rho_0\in[\delta,1]$, there are $\rho\in[\rho_0,A\rho_0)$ and $\rho$-tubes $\mathcal T_\rho$ such that:
(i) $\mathcal T_\rho$ is an $A$-uniform partitioning cover of $\mathcal T$;
(ii) for each parent, the unit-rescaled child family satisfies the convex Wolff axiom with error $A$.
This is the root hypothesis; neither a direction-separated cover nor self-similar child counts is stipulated.
nodes.correspondence: This is the public nearby-scale predicate, including essential distinctness and complete containment fibres. Only the requested scale is bounded by one; the selected scale may exceed one.

nodes.roadmap_statement:
If $\mathcal T$ satisfies the multi-scale convex Wolff axiom with error $A$, then for every $\rho_0\in[\delta,1]$ one can choose $\rho\in[\rho_0,A\rho_0]$ and a $\rho$-cover whose coarse family and every unit-rescaled child family satisfy the same multi-scale condition with error $O(A)$.
Partitioning forces the child-incidence clusters at successive scales to form a nested tree.
nodes.correspondence: This is a mathematical inheritance interface. No standalone proof of the displayed general inheritance lemma is linked. The closed structural theorem reconstructs its particular covers and fibres; the expert inheritance arrows do not establish arbitrary refinement closure.

nodes.roadmap_statement:
Let $\mathsf{Bad}(s)$ mean: for every $\eta,\delta_0>0$, some $0<\delta\le\delta_0$ has multi-scale convex Wolff error $\delta^{-\eta}$, shading density $\delta^\eta$, and $|E_C|\le\delta^s$.
Define $\sigma=\sigma_{\rm CW}=\sup(\{0\}\cup\{s>0:\mathsf{Bad}(s)\})$.
Failure of Theorem 5.2 gives $\sigma>0$. This is a new deficit for a different admissible class, not WZ1's $\sigma_3$.
nodes.correspondence: Lean defines admissibility globally and chooses its supremum locally inside critical extraction. There is no separately exported constant sigma_CW identified with the directional WZ1 exponent.

nodes.roadmap_statement:
Write $E_C=\bigcup_TY(T)$ and $\sigma=\sigma_{\rm CW}$. The pair $C=(\mathcal T,Y)_\delta$ is \emph{$\varepsilon$-CW-extremal} precisely when
\[\begin{aligned}
&\mathcal T\text{ satisfies multi-scale convex Wolff with error }\delta^{-\varepsilon},\\
&\sum_T|Y(T)|\ge\delta^\varepsilon\sum_T|T|,\\
&|E_C|\le\delta^{\sigma-\varepsilon}.
\end{aligned}\]
This is WZ2 Definition 6.1, where it is called $\varepsilon$-extremal. The added CW label distinguishes it from WZ1's different extremal class.
nodes.correspondence: The Lean extremal configuration stores nonemptiness, nearby-scale CWA, aggregate shading density, and the volume upper bound. Its critical exponent is supplied explicitly.

Let $C,f,V$ satisfy Proposition 6.4 with loss $\eta$. Let $\delta^{1/2}\le|J|\le\delta^\varepsilon$.
Assume $\sum_T|Y(T)\cap(\mathbb R^2\times J)|\ge\delta^\eta|J|$ and that the shaded union in this slab is covered by at most $\delta^{-\eta}|J|^{-2+\sigma}$ cubes of side $|J|$.
For sufficiently small $\eta,\delta_0$ one has $|f'(z)|\ge|J|$ for every $z\in J$.
nodes.correspondence: The prepared interval theorem remains the actual Proposition 6.5 dependency, and its original interface is preserved. Its core now needs frame control only on the retained slab. It has no frame premise and does not choose another C2 configuration. The occupied-cell hull preserves the original slab mass; dense short-grain selection retains half its mass on the same family, and local AD plus the tube-segment direction estimate proves frame nondegeneracy. All cutoffs precede the configuration and interval. This independently audited API still needs normalized mass and a fine cap, neither derived from the printed absolute delta^eta |J| hypothesis and cover alone. The closed every-interval C2 source now supplies only the global cap before J and calls this new lemma; the older global-frame source and prescribed-frame theorem remain separately audited compatibility APIs. nodes.roadmap_statement:
If $\sigma>0$, apply the lower bound with exponent $\sigma/4$.
Choose the small-image construction with loss $\kappa<\sigma/4$ and $\kappa$ smaller than the lower-bound admissibility threshold.
At arbitrarily small mesh the same pair obeys
$\delta^{\sigma/4}\le |X_f(C)|\lesssim\delta^{\sigma-\kappa}$,
which is impossible. Therefore $\sigma_{\rm CW}=0$.
nodes.correspondence: The contradiction primary fixes the proved normalized Lemma 6.7 internally and takes only a positive critical package. The argument-free final theorem calls this contradiction and retains exactly its original statement. Both the Lemma 6.7-to-contradiction and contradiction-to-final connections are therefore actual proof-value dependencies. It compares both bounds on the actual normalized left terminal. The independent lower bound follows CWA to finite length-32 coarse-capsule tests to corrected Proposition 7.1, then the complete parameter iteration. The upper family, shading and slope are the same literal data, and the lower loss and cutoff precede the terminal choice. The generic upper-parameter and common-height contradiction interfaces remain independently proved; neither intermediate side invokes a final theorem.
